deviations.what: the terminal drain must fire at drive end on every exit reason, not only when a forced synthesis turn fires — and at least one in-repo host must wire append_guidance so delivered counsel actually reaches the cortex
deviations.reason: measured by task t4 during implementation: _maybe_force_synthesis returns early when the model finished cleanly with a non-empty summary, so a clean-finish drive produces ZERO terminal boundaries and the t4 fix never fires; the baseline series that measured one late drop per run (4 of 4) looks like clean finishes, so as scoped the fix would not address the failure it was written for and c22 honesty could pass vacuously. Separately, no checked-in host (greenhouse, league_seat, proof) wires append_guidance, so counsel lands on _noop_guidance and cannot reach the synthesis messages in a live run.

deviations.what: ThreadedMuseRunner cannot carry a tool bench, so tools are unreachable inside a live drive and t20 (flip default-on) has nothing to flip; a new task t26 adds the runner seam
deviations.reason: measured by t16: muse_runner.py:596-602 constructs MuseLoop with no tools= argument, so no supported path puts a bench inside a live drive. The tool seam (t10), the pad (t12) and the workspace (t13) are all reachable only by a harness constructing MuseLoop directly. Arm C therefore remains measurable at harness level (t17/t18) but tools cannot ship in a drive, and the default-on flip q6 authorised is not executable as specified.

deviations.reason: plan defect in my own task instruction: t18 was told to classify arm C executions "by the rule already fixed in t6 prereg", but t6 produced devague-legs-preregistration.md for the two-mind experiment and contains no execution-classification rule. deviations.what: the arm harness adds a closing turn: one tools-off constant appended to the muse own message history, put to every arm alike
deviations.reason: smoke-driven and not named in the plan or issue 21: handed a pad, the muse emitted finish_reason=tool_calls with EMPTY content on all 8 turns (6 pad writes, zero prose), so arms B and C returned NO_ANSWER every run and DV1 was measuring the turn budget rather than correctness. The closing turn is asked once, tools-off, from the muse's real history, never after a transport failure. It changes the answer-extraction protocol for all three arms, so it is recorded rather than left for t18 to discover.

deviations.what: muse tools do NOT flip default-on: they stay opt-in, and t20 becomes the record of why
deviations.reason: the operator's q6 decision was 'validation first, then default-on ships with the tuned protocol — the measured failure mode never ships as default behaviour'. t18's pre-registered series (24 runs, n=8 per arm, 0 transport failures) returned INCONCLUSIVE at an arm-A ceiling AND measured new harm: tools-off answered 8/8 correct with 0 NO_ANSWER, while the tool arms produced 9 NO_ANSWER across 16 runs, a 74% workspace-call refusal rate (17 of 23 argv malformed), and 17 open intents in arm C. By the operator's own stated rule, that is a measured failure mode and must not ship as the default. Flipping would ship a configuration the evidence says is worse.

deviations.what: add a new experiment: full-Gemma vs full-Qwen homogeneous model arms across an escalating-difficulty League of Agents ladder, to decide whether to consolidate to one model
deviations.reason: operator request 2026-07-31. The question no experiment in this cycle answers: every run so far uses the MIXED pairing (Qwen cortex + Gemma muse), so nothing measures whether a single model would do as well or better. t9 already showed the muse reaching identical verdicts to the cortex for about 1/25 the completion tokens and 1/10 the wall clock, which makes consolidation a live economic question rather than a hypothetical. Escalating difficulty is also the direct fix for the ceiling that made association-work, arena-series and muse-arms all INCONCLUSIVE: the ladder keeps rising until the arms separate or the ladder runs out.

deviations.what: the model-consolidation experiment is a round-robin head-to-head, not three solo runs against the house bot: gemma-vs-mixed, mixed-vs-qwen, qwen-vs-gemma
deviations.reason: operator refinement 2026-07-31. Head-to-head answers "which is better" directly rather than inferring it from three separate scores against a shared scripted opponent. It requires harness work: league_seat.py drives the rival with rival_orders(), a deterministic scripted policy (lines 1449, 1592), not a model — so both teams must be driven by model seats. The cli.act(match_id, team, orders) seam is symmetric, so this is feasible beside league_seat.py rather than inside it.

deviations.reason: additive and labelled post-hoc in code — absent from ARMS, excluded from --arm all. deviations.what: add an architecture experiment: Gemma as top-level coordinator with final authority delegating to a Qwen subagent developer, against today actor-plus-advisor arrangement and a mirror arm
deviations.reason: operator proposal 2026-07-31. Verified expressible today with no embodiment change: loop.run takes complete (this level model) and subagent: SubagentFn = Callable[[SubagentCall], Optional[SubagentResult]], so the HOST drives the child and picks its model — subagent.py documents passing allowance/max_steps/lineage through as "the whole protocol". It also maps onto colleague 352 framing, which already frames cortex only on the top-level acting loop and types subagents separately. The proposal changes TWO variables against today at once — who holds final authority (Qwen to Gemma) and whether the second model executes or advises (Gemma advising to Qwen executing) — so a mirror arm is required to attribute any effect.

deviations.what: t28 is rescoped from an abstract coordinator-plus-developer experiment to the concrete League of Agents instantiation: Gemma commands, Qwen drives the unit agents, on the continuous lane
deviations.reason: operator instantiation 2026-07-31, and the arena supports it natively — verified: league cmatch is the continuous lane and asks for exactly ONE unit's action at a decision point, where the grid lane asks for a whole-team turn order, so the commander/unit split is native rather than simulated. league team register --agent ID:MODEL:ROLE declares a model per unit, giving the arena its own fairness record of which model played which unit. c-skirmish-1 exists and validates roster roles (defender, harvester). Rescoping rather than adding t29 avoids two overlapping tasks for one question.

deviations.what: design decisions taken under delegated authority for t28: continuous lane over grid lane, four arms with two flat baselines, house bot as the fixed opponent, and per-level token accounting
deviations.reason: the operator delegated further decisions to me rather than being asked. (1) Continuous lane, because cmatch asks per-unit natively. (2) Arms: B Gemma-commands-Qwen-units (the proposal), C the mirror Qwen-commands-Gemma-units, plus flat single-model baselines — the mirror separates architecture from model assignment, and a flat baseline is what says whether hierarchy helps at all. (3) A fixed house-bot opponent rather than hierarchy-vs-hierarchy, because t27 already covers head-to-head at team level and doubling the arms again would not finish. (4) Tokens reported per LEVEL, since the question is whether a large commander pays for itself.

deviations.what: the reference rig consolidates on Qwen as the only actor: cortex Qwen 3.6 27B, senses Gemma 4 12B for intake and speak-back, and the Gemma 4 31B muse not used — the muse stays a shipped opt-in seam, off by default, not deleted code

deviations.what: raise the shipped cortex token default from 2048 to 16000 in the example hosts, as a direct consequence of t24 and d15: with Qwen the only actor, the budget t24 measured as silently truncating 6.0% of completions is now the budget every act runs at
deviations.reason: decision taken under delegated authority 2026-07-31. t24 measured 5 of 83 completions truncating at 2048 with zero degradations recorded, because ModelResponse carries no finish_reason (issue #37) — a truncated turn and a deliberate one are the same object at the seam. At 16000: 0 of 58. d15 removes the muse, so the cortex is the only mind that can lose a turn this way. The measured value stays recorded in arena-budget.md so the series' instrument is not made retroactively unreadable by the change it caused

deviations.what: headspace-cli>=0.11 enters as the fourth base dependency: the version floor is 0.11 precisely because 0.11.0 is the release that answered d2's open condition — headspace.api became the declared public surface under headspace's own semver, with headspace.core private (headspace-cli#18, closed by them)
deviations.reason: d2 recorded the conditional (import at module scope only if the Python API is declared public, otherwise subprocess the CLI) but nothing recorded how it resolved, so the ledger did not name the dependency, its floor, or the justification. Resolution: 0.10.0 advertised only __version__ in __all__, which is why the condition existed; 0.11.0 declares create/run/put/export/destroy on headspace.api, so the import path is the one taken and the floor cannot go below 0.11. Costs measured rather than assumed — install adds docker>=7.1 plus requests, urllib3, certifi, charset-normalizer, idna; 'import headspace.api' pulls stdlib only, so the runtime-import set gains exactly one entry while docker and requests stay install-only. Pinned in three places that move together or the gate is red: pyproject.toml, _APPROVED_DEPENDENCIES and _REQUIRED_RUNTIME_IMPORTS in tests/test_zero_deps.py. Filed by the Qodo reviewer on PR #38 as a compliance gap in the audit trail, and it was one
